dimensions.name: Requirements and scope
dimensions.description: Clarifies conversation types, delivery guarantees, multi-device behavior, and what is out of scope.

levels.1: Repeats the prompt without defining delivery guarantees or device behavior.
levels.2: Lists the features but ignores ordering, offline delivery, or multi-device sync.
levels.3: Separates functional and non-functional requirements and states latency, durability, and ordering assumptions.
levels.4: Also quantifies acceptable duplicate delivery, explains the push fallback, and names the assumptions about media and encryption.

dimensions.name: Protocol and message envelope
dimensions.description: Defines the realtime protocol, message fields, acknowledgements, and history APIs.

levels.1: No clear protocol or message shape.
levels.2: Defines a send call but omits acknowledgements, idempotency, or history.
levels.3: Defines a message envelope with a client id, acknowledgements, and history pagination.
levels.4: Also covers reconnect cursors, receipt events, typing/presence events, and versioning of the protocol.

dimensions.name: Ordering and storage
dimensions.description: Chooses a per-conversation sequence, message schema, partitioning, and storage engine.

levels.1: No concrete message schema or ordering model.
levels.2: Stores messages but orders by timestamp or has no partitioning plan.
levels.3: Defines a per-conversation sequence and a schema partitioned by conversation and time.
levels.4: Also discusses hot conversations, retention, receipts storage, and how a conversation moves between shards.

dimensions.name: Delivery architecture
dimensions.description: Separates connection management, persistence, fan-out, push, and sync.

levels.1: A single server that both stores and delivers messages.
levels.2: Names a chat service and a socket layer but does not show the send or delivery flow.
levels.3: Shows the send path, connection registry, fan-out, offline push, and reconnect sync.
levels.4: Also explains why each component scales independently and how the online and offline paths converge.

dimensions.name: Scale and performance
dimensions.description: Sizes connections, message throughput, fan-out, and history reads.

levels.1: Ignores the stated message volume or connection count.
levels.2: Repeats the numbers without estimating QPS, fan-out, or storage.
levels.3: Estimates message QPS, connection counts, storage, and group fan-out.
levels.4: Also quantifies delivery latency, fan-out lag, hot-group mitigation, and the cost of retaining history.

dimensions.name: Trade-offs
dimensions.description: Compares ordering, delivery, and fan-out choices and defends the selected guarantees.

levels.2: Names at-least-once or push delivery without connecting it to the design.
levels.3: Compares at least two meaningful choices, such as single-writer sequencing vs distributed ids or fan-out on write vs read.
levels.4: Also explains when the chosen guarantee is insufficient and what would trigger a redesign.

dimensions.name: Failure modes and operations
dimensions.description: Covers disconnects, duplicate delivery, storage outages, and the metrics that reveal them.

levels.1: Assumes connections and storage never fail.
levels.2: Mentions reconnect or retries without a recovery path.
levels.3: Identifies the main failure modes and the metrics or alerts that detect them.
levels.4: Also covers resume cursors, duplicate suppression, sequencer hot spots, push outages, and runbook-level recovery.
